summary: Recommends that Internet-facing servers log the source port number and accurate timestamps, not just the client IP address. Address sharing after IPv4 exhaustion means many users can share one address, so the port and time are needed to identify who did what. This is a best current practice.

eli5.summary: If a whole street shares one mailbox address, a letter needs an apartment number to show who sent it. This says servers should write down the port and the exact time too, not only the address.

questions: what is carrier grade nat logging
subtitle: Servers that log client IP addresses should also log source port and an accurate timestamp.

tldr.problem: After IPv4 exhaustion, service providers share one public IPv4 address among many customers, so an address alone no longer identifies who made a connection.
tldr.mechanism: Internet-facing servers that log incoming IP addresses should also log the source port, a timestamp accurate to the second from a traceable time source, and the transport protocol and destination port when needed.
tldr.outcome: Operators of address sharing can then match a logged connection to a single subscriber when handling abuse or public safety requests.

facts.label: Timestamp accuracy
facts.value: To the second or better, in UTC

today: RFC 6302 is Best Current Practice 162 and has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why Addresses Alone Are Not Enough
sections.content:
The global IPv4 address free pool at IANA was exhausted in February 2011. Providers will often have little choice but to share IPv4 global addresses among multiple customers, using address translation or sharing such as NAT44, NAT64 or DS-Lite.

In the past, knowing the external global IP address was enough to identify a subscriber of interest. With address sharing, the external public address of a session alone is no longer enough to identify customers unambiguously. The document is about logging on servers, not about logging on carrier-grade NAT or other address sharing tools.
sections.eli5: Many families now use the same front door number, so the number alone does not say which family knocked.

sections.title: What Servers Should Log
sections.content:
It is RECOMMENDED as best current practice that Internet-facing servers that log incoming IP addresses also log:

  • The source port number.
  • A timestamp, RECOMMENDED in UTC, accurate to the second, from a traceable time source such as NTP.
  • The transport protocol (usually TCP or UDP) and destination port number, when the server application uses multiple transports or ports.

Examples of such servers include web servers and email servers. The advice also applies to devices such as load-balancers that log incoming connections on behalf of actual servers, and to both IPv4 and IPv6, if only for consistency and code simplification.
sections.eli5: Along with the sender's address, write down which numbered slot they used and exactly what time it was.

sections.title: Timestamps and Port Reuse
sections.content:
Carrier-grade NATs may have different policies to recycle ports. Some may reuse a port almost immediately, others may wait several minutes. Servers cannot know how fast ports will be reused, so they should log timestamps using a reasonably accurate clock; the recommended accuracy is to the second or better.

UTC is preferred to local time with an offset or time zone, because the extra information can be lost in the reporting chain. The recommendations do not require any change in which packets are examined and logged. Data-retention policies are out of scope, although protecting logs matters: if logs are tampered with, evidence could be destroyed.
sections.eli5: The same slot number can be handed to someone else a moment later, so the exact time is what tells the two apart.

sections.title: ISPs and Security Considerations
sections.content:
ISPs deploying address sharing should also deploy a logging architecture that records the relation between a customer's identity and the IP and port resources used, but recommendations on that are out of scope.

The security consideration is that without the source port and accurate timestamp, operators using address sharing will not be able to identify customers unambiguously when dealing with abuse or public safety queries.
sections.eli5: Without the slot number and the time, nobody can tell which family to ask when something goes wrong.
